input:
Write a bash script that rotates numbered log files.

Starting files in /home/eval/logs (nothing else is in that directory):
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log ---
line c
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.1 ---
line b
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.2 ---
line a
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.3 ---
line 0
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/app.log.old ---
manual backup
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/worker.log ---
w2
--- end ---
--- /home/eval/logs/worker.log.1 ---
w1
--- end ---

Define a shell function `rotate LOGFILE KEEP` implementing classic numbered rotation:
- `LOGFILE.N` becomes `LOGFILE.N+1` for every existing N, highest first, so nothing is overwritten.
- Afterwards no numbered file above KEEP may remain (delete any that would end up numbered higher than KEEP).
- `LOGFILE` itself becomes `LOGFILE.1`, and a new empty `LOGFILE` is created.
- Files that are not exactly `LOGFILE` or `LOGFILE.<number>` (for example `app.log.old`) must not be touched.

Then call it twice: `rotate /home/eval/logs/app.log 3` and `rotate /home/eval/logs/worker.log 2`. Exit 0.

transcript.final_response:
The script below defines `rotate` and calls it on both logs.

**Expected result:**

| Log | After rotation |
|---|---|
| `app.log` | new and empty |
| `app.log.1` | `line c` |
| `app.log.2` | `line b` |
| `app.log.3` | `line a` |
| `app.log.old` | unchanged |
| `line 0` (old `app.log.3`) | deleted |
| `worker.log` | new and empty |
| `worker.log.1` | `w2` |
| `worker.log.2` | `w1` |

**How `rotate` handles the cases:**
- **Finding numbered files:** only names whose suffix is all digits count. Names like `app.log.old` are skipped and never touched.
- **Order:** files are renamed from the highest number down, so no file overwrites another.
- **Deleting old files:** any file whose new number would be above KEEP is deleted instead of renamed.
- **The live log:** `LOGFILE` moves to `.1`. If KEEP is 0 it is removed instead. A new empty `LOGFILE` is then created.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

rotate() {
    local logfile="$1" keep="$2"
    local f suffix n
    local -a nums=()

    for f in "$logfile".*; do
        [[ -e "$f" ]] || continue
        suffix="${f#"$logfile".}"
        if [[ "$suffix" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
            nums+=("$suffix")
        fi
    done

    if (( ${#nums[@]} > 0 )); then
        local sorted
        sorted=$(printf '%s\n' "${nums[@]}" | sort -rn)
        while IFS= read -r suffix; do
            [[ -n "$suffix" ]] || continue
            n=$((10#$suffix))
            if (( n + 1 > keep )); then
                rm -f -- "$logfile.$suffix"
            else
                mv -f -- "$logfile.$suffix" "$logfile.$((n + 1))"
            fi
        done <<< "$sorted"
    fi

    if [[ -e "$logfile" ]]; then
        if (( keep >= 1 )); then
            mv -f -- "$logfile" "$logfile.1"
        else
            rm -f -- "$logfile"
        fi
    fi
    : > "$logfile"
}

rotate /home/eval/logs/app.log 3
rotate /home/eval/logs/worker.log 2
exit 0
```
